olivia: Hey team — since ~2026-03-15T14:02Z our p50 for text-generation requests jumped from ~120ms to ~600ms and we started seeing intermittent 502s. Impacting API v1/generate with ~80 concurrent clients. Example response headers: `x-rw-request-id: rw_req_20260315_01`, `x-rw-request-id: rw_req_20260315_02`. Can you help with repro steps?

emma: Sorry for the trouble — we'll take this. Can you share the exact request IDs (you posted two, but we may need several spanning the incident window), a short prompt set (5-10 prompts that hit the issue), peak concurrency number, typical prompt token count and expected response token count, and whether you're on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private? Also please run the following curl to capture a single failing request and include the full raw response (headers + body):

```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.3-large","input":"<one of your prompts>"}' 
```

We only need the response headers (especially `x-rw-request-id` and `x-rw-trace-id`) and the HTTP status code. If you can paste 3-5 examples that hit the 502s that'd be ideal.

support-bot: Ticket created: INC-2026-4872 — adding eng-runtime and eng-sre.

ajay: Quick ask from runtime side: which model variant / quantization are you using, and are you pinning to a specific revision? Also, is this on Hosted (multi-tenant) or Redwood Dedicated? Hypothesis: if prefix KV cache misses align with high concurrency + long prompts we can see latency amplification. If you can also export a short sample of the model config (sequence length, kv-cache-enabled flag, any custom max_new_tokens) that helps.

kevin: From infra: please run a short stress repro with `wrk` or `fortio` so we can see the 502 / p50 behavior locally. Example `wrk` command we use for repro: 

```bash
# approximate 80 concurrent clients with 60s run
wrk -t8 -c80 -d60s -s post.lua --latency https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/generate
# post.lua posts JSON body with Authorization header, see internal snippet in the ticket
```

If you can't run `wrk`, `hey` or `ab` is fine. Capture the full response headers and save stdout/stderr. Also if possible collect a debug bundle using the support helper: `rw-support collect-debug --request-ids rw_req_20260315_01 rw_req_20260315_02 --out debug-olivia-20260315.zip` and upload the resulting archive here. That bundle will include client traces and server-side trace snippets we need.

olivia: Thanks — details below.
- deployment: Hosted API (region: us-west-2)
- model: `redwood-1.3-large` (default hosted quantization)
- peak concurrency: ~80 concurrent connections, sustained ~30s bursts
- typical prompt tokens: 130-170 tokens
- typical response tokens: 120-260 tokens
- sample request ids (span of incident): `rw_req_20260315_01`, `rw_req_20260315_03`, `rw_req_20260315_07`
- small promptset (3 examples):
  1) "Summarize: The product launch cadence for Q2 ... (100 token context)"
  2) "Write an outline for a 600-word blog post about model serving economics."
  3) "Refactor: Given this JS function, return an optimized variant. [code block]"

I ran the curl you posted; got one of the 502s. Raw response header excerpt: `HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`, `x-rw-request-id: rw_req_20260315_03`, `x-rw-trace-id: trace-7a9f2`. Full verb output attached as `curl-rw_req_20260315_03.txt` in the ticket. I'm happy to run `wrk` if you give the exact body to post.

emma: Perfect — thanks Olivia. Can you run the support collector as `rw-support collect-debug --request-ids rw_req_20260315_01 rw_req_20260315_03 rw_req_20260315_07 --include-metrics --out debug-olivia-20260315.zip` and drop the zip here? That will give us server trace snippets, GPU scheduling logs, and the request-level latency breakdowns. If you can't run it we can do a live session. Also please run a short `wrk` with this minimal JSON body (replace <PROMPT> with one of your short prompts):

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-1.3-large",
  "input": "<PROMPT>",
  "max_new_tokens": 250
}
```

Use `wrk` or `fortio`; aim for 80 concurrent clients for 30s to reproduce. Share the `wrk` latencies and stderr.

ajay: I'll try to reproduce on a dev cluster with the promptset + concurrency. If I get 502s I'll attach the runtime logs; if it's only p50 bump we may be looking at batching thresholds or KV cache eviction under memory pressure.

kevin: Once we have the debug zip and the `wrk` output I'll correlate with infra metrics (GPU util, mem, qps per shard) and check autoscaler events around the timestamp. If autoscaler didn't scale because of a sticky rolling update that could explain transient 502s.

olivia: Uploaded `debug-olivia-20260315.zip` and `wrk-output-80c-30s.log` to the ticket, also included the curl verboselog. Let me know if you need screen share to run anything in my environment.

emma: Received, thanks. I'll triage the debug bundle now and will paste the first-pass findings in this thread in ~30-45m.

kevin: Noted — I'm pulling the infra dashboards for us-west-2 for 2026-03-15T13:50..14:10Z.

ajay: I'll start a local run with the 3 prompts and 80 concurrency against our staging runtime to try and reproduce. Will post any stack traces or runtime logs here.

emma: (thumbsup)
